claim: Alissa, Sim & Hart propose feature-free algorithm selection using recurrent neural networks (LSTM/GRU) trained on raw instance sequences to select among heuristics/solvers, contrasting with typical feature-based algorithm selection requiring hand-derived instance features -- the neural network here is the SELECTOR, not a surrogate objective model.
stance_target: algorithm-selection literature's use of neural networks targets solver/heuristic selection, not surrogate-model selection
scope_conditions: online bin-packing, selecting among four well-known packing heuristics
quoted_support: we train two types of recurrent neural networks to predict a packing heuristic in online bin-packing, selecting from four well-known heuristics. As input, the RNN methods only use the sequence of item-sizes.
numbers: within 5% of oracle performance on 80.88% to 97.63% of instances, depending on dataset

claim: The word 'surrogate' does not appear anywhere in this 2023 Journal of Heuristics survey of feature-based vs. feature-free algorithm selection, and 'landscape' appears only twice, both in bibliography citations (to Kerschke et al.'s ELA survey and a MAX-SAT landscape paper) rather than in the main text's methodology.
stance_target: modern algorithm-selection surveys discuss surrogate-model selection
scope_conditions: full-text search of the 2023 survey (approx. 15,573 words extracted)
quoted_support: bining exploratory landscape analysis and machine learning. Evol. Comput. 27(1), 99-127 (2019)

claim: The survey restates Rice's (1976) algorithm-selection framework as its foundational reference point for both feature-based and feature-free approaches, confirming Rice's framework (mapping instances to algorithms/solvers) remains the field's core paradigm as of 2023.
stance_target: the canonical algorithm-selection framework targets solver/optimizer choice
quoted_support: the design and selection of features to describe an instance. Two deep-neural networks

claim: Feature-free RNN-based selectors are shown to outperform classical machine learning models trained on hand-engineered instance features for the online bin-packing selection task.
stance_target: comparative performance of feature-free vs. feature-based algorithm selection
